prompt: What does white-box testing use to choose its tests?

choices.text: The code’s structure
choices.why: Right: its decisions, branches and paths.

choices.text: The requirement, read one sentence at a time and turned into a table of cases
choices.why: That is lesson 6’s black-box method.

choices.text: Customer complaints from the counter
choices.why: That is where lesson 4 started.

choices.text: A random sample of inputs
choices.why: Random inputs ignore the structure.

prompt: Which defect can white-box testing find that black-box testing from the rule cannot?

choices.text: A time without a leading zero being mispriced
choices.why: Lesson 4 found that from outside.

choices.text: A missing check that would refuse a negative age, which the rule never asked for
choices.why: Missing code is what white box cannot see.

choices.text: A sixty-year-old charged full price
choices.why: Lesson 1 found that from the rule.

choices.text: A line that gives a discount on one date no rule mentions
choices.why: Right: the line exists, so reading or coverage finds it.

prompt: Match each coverage criterion to when it is satisfied.

pairs.right: every part of a combined decision was true and false
every route to a return has been taken

prompt: A tester who cannot program is asked to do white-box testing of `tickets.py`. By this lesson, what do they need?

choices.text: A paid tool
choices.why: Python’s own trace module does it.

choices.text: To read the code well enough to ask the questions, and a tool that records what ran
choices.why: Right: nobody has to change a line.

choices.text: To rewrite it first, in a language they already know well enough
choices.why: Reading is enough.

choices.text: Nothing: white box is only for developers
choices.why: The lesson argues the reading part is a tester’s skill.

prompt: With the six cases, what percentage of `tickets.py`’s lines did trace report as run?
What does `>>>>>>` mean in front of a line of the `.cover` file?

choices.text: The line failed
choices.why: Coverage does not check results.

choices.text: The line is a comment
choices.why: Comments carry no mark.

choices.text: The line never ran
choices.why: Right: `--missing` marks it.

choices.text: The line ran more than a hundred times during the tests
choices.why: Counts are written as numbers.

prompt: `brl` and the last two lines of `tickets.py` never ran under `cases.py`. Why is that not a gap in the testing?

choices.text: trace ignores functions
choices.why: It counted `price`, a function.

choices.text: Because 83% is above the industry’s accepted minimum for coverage
choices.why: There is no such minimum, and the number is not the argument.

choices.text: They are the command-line part, which lesson 6 already ran from outside
choices.why: Right: not every unrun line is a gap; the report needs reading.

choices.text: Those lines cannot contain defects
choices.why: Any line can; these were tested another way.

prompt: Which line of `price` did the six cases from lesson 6 never run?

choices.text: The Wednesday half, which runs just on the cheapest day of the week
choices.why: The Wednesday adult ran it.

choices.text: The matinée price
choices.why: The 16:59 case ran it.

choices.text: The reduction for people over sixty
choices.why: Right: no case was over sixty.

choices.text: The student reduction
choices.why: The student of 20 ran it.

prompt: After the sixty-one-year-old is added, every line of `price` has run and all seven cases pass. What does that prove about the sixty-year-old?

choices.text: That sixty is charged half, because the line that gives the reduction ran
choices.why: It ran for sixty-one; for sixty it is skipped.

choices.text: That the defect was fixed
choices.why: No code changed.

choices.text: That coverage tools are broken
choices.why: The tool reported exactly what ran.

choices.text: Nothing: sixty was never tried
choices.why: Right: the defect is still there with full statement coverage.

prompt: With seven cases, every decision in `price` went both ways. What is still untested?

choices.text: Each decision on its false side
choices.why: Every decision was false at least once.

choices.text: Combinations of decisions
choices.why: Right: full branch coverage, and the stacking path never taken.

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: Both defects are still in the code.

choices.text: The `else` of the session decision
choices.why: Five cases took it.

prompt: How many combinations of session, student, age group and Wednesday does the lesson count for `price`?
hint: Two times two times three times two.

prompt: Why does nobody aim for full path coverage in real programs?
hint: Each independent decision doubles the count.

choices.text: Paths multiply too fast to cover
choices.why: Right: twenty independent decisions already give over a million.

choices.text: Paths are irrelevant to defects
choices.why: The stacking defect lived in an untaken path.

choices.text: Branch coverage already includes every path
choices.why: Full branch coverage left both defects in place.

choices.text: Tools cannot measure paths
choices.why: The objection is the count, not the tooling.

prompt: What does path thinking give a tester instead of a target?

choices.text: A reason to skip black box
choices.why: The two are used together.

choices.text: A way of asking where to look
choices.why: Right: which decisions interact, and which combinations nobody tried.

choices.text: A complete list of tests to write
choices.why: The list is too long to write.

choices.text: A percentage to report each sprint to the product owner, alongside the defects found
choices.why: Exactly what it is not.

prompt: In which direction does a coverage report never lie?

choices.text: A line that ran is a line that was checked
choices.why: Running is not checking.

choices.text: A higher number always means better tests than a lower one
choices.why: Assertions and inputs are invisible to the number.

choices.text: A line that never ran is a line nobody tested
choices.why: Right: use it to find what has not been tested.

choices.text: 100% means the code is correct
choices.why: The other direction, and false.

prompt: Which of these can a coverage report not tell you? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: whether the result of a line was checked
choices.why: Yes: execution, not checking.

choices.text: whether a line ran
choices.why: No: that is exactly what it tells.

choices.text: whether the values at the edges were tried
choices.why: Yes: sixty-one ran the line, sixty was never asked for.

choices.text: whether code is missing
choices.why: Yes: it measures only lines that exist.

prompt: Why is the leading-zero defect invisible to every coverage criterion?

choices.text: No line handles the format
choices.why: Right: missing code leaves no trace in the structure.

choices.text: It only happens on Sundays
choices.why: Lesson 4 ruled Sunday out.

choices.text: trace skips lines that contain strings
choices.why: It counts lines whatever they contain.

choices.text: The line `if time < "17:00"` never ran
choices.why: It ran in every case.

prompt: Order the coverage criteria from least strict to most strict.
trap: Each is satisfied by more tests than the one before it.
